static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.family_status: Lives with two dogs, no other family members
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends who can provide emotional support, but has not yet discussed work difficulties with them; relationships with colleagues are affected by frequently seeking reassurance from them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior experience of similar psychological problems, has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, cooperative attitude but negative tone; repeated self-doubt, often uses catastrophic and black-and-white expressions; tends to seek external reassurance

basic_info.main_problem: I feel incompetent in my accounting work, especially after making an error balancing the books, with persistent self-doubt and anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: Self-doubt and anxiety are affecting work performance and overall physical and mental health; hopes to reduce anxiety and self-doubt through counseling and restore work functioning.
growth_experiences: A few weeks ago, he made a major error balancing accounts at work; since then he persistently doubts his own abilities and feels anxious during work hours and when facing accounting tasks; he believes high workload and performance pressure may be triggers. To relieve his emotions he tried repeated checking, seeking reassurance from colleagues, and short breaks, but with limited effect, resulting in affected sleep and diet, and tense relationships with colleagues due to frequent verification-seeking.

Before the mistake, his work performance was generally good and he had received praise from his supervisor; but when anxious, he finds it hard to recall and acknowledge this positive evidence, feeling 'that was long ago and has nothing to do with now'.

special_situations.event: Making a major mistake when balancing the accounts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make an error on important accounts, it means I am not suited to this job / should not continue working as an accountant
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checking, seeking reassurance from colleagues, trying to avoid high-risk tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a failure; if this goes on I will be fired

special_situations.event: Facing accounting-related tasks during work hours
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I handle the accounts again, I will very likely make mistakes again; I must achieve zero errors to be safe
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pausing and postponing high-risk tasks, prioritizing low-risk or smaller tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am going to mess up again; something will definitely go wrong

special_situations.event: Realizing one received praise from a supervisor in the past
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past success does not represent present ability; once a recent mistake is made, past achievements no longer count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Discounting positive evidence, focusing only on recent mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those praises do not count; now I am worthless

special_situations.event: Interacting with supervisors or colleagues, or thinking about how they view oneself
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others will judge me definitively by one mistake; if others do not affirm me immediately, it means they think I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently seeking confirmation and putting oneself down in conversation to lower others' expectations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am incompetent

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as competent, to be trusted, and to gain a sense of security
core_conflict.fear: Fears being negated, criticized, or fired due to mistakes, thereby losing relationships and a sense of worth
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of making mistakes through excessive caution, repeated checking, and seeking reassurance from others, avoiding negative evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: A subordinate who is incompetent, error-prone, and needs others to double-check
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges / superiors or colleagues who find fault at any moment

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When assigned or beginning to handle important account tasks
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets the attention of supervisors / colleagues as scrutiny and negation, as if they are waiting for them to make a mistake
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Appears nervous, speech rate quickens, constantly explains and self-justifies, and frequently asks 'is this okay / is there a problem'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes behavioral experiments or positive hypotheses
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting suggestions as implying one is incompetent and must be corrected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a pragmatic tone, emphasizes 'the real problem is the workload is too big' and 'these methods are useless', avoiding discussing feelings in depth.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling that accounting error and evaluating oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating one mistake with overall incompetence and failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses self-deprecating wording (such as 'I should not be doing this job'), lowers the volume, and reduces eye contact.

manifestations: Does not discuss work troubles with friends; bears the stress alone
Relationships with colleagues are strained due to frequent verification seeking, experiencing interpersonal distance
In work settings, feels alone in facing the risk of mistakes and judgment
outcomes: Decreased work efficiency, avoiding high-risk tasks

manifestations: Marked pressure about choices and actions requiring bearing consequences (such as being fired for mistakes)
Hopes to gain a sense of safety through 'zero errors', leading to excessive caution and hesitation
outcomes: Avoids high-risk tasks; inner tension and conflict increase

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeated self-blame (such as 'I should not be doing this job' 'I do not trust myself')
Excessively careful in doing things, prone to negating one's own ability

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Believing supervisors and colleagues will equate one mistake with one's overall incompetence
Attributes the inner experience of self-criticism to others' hypothetical evaluations of them, and thus frequently seeks reassurance

positive_force: Has had past experiences of competence and received positive feedback from his supervisor
Willing to try structured behavioral experiments, with a certain willingness to cooperate
Has some social support resources (has friends to confide in)
negative_force: Significant cognitive distortions: catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, disqualifying the positive, fortune telling, labeling
High workload and performance pressure intensify the fear of making mistakes
Relies on external confirmation (frequent verification-seeking) and repeated checking to maintain the anxiety cycle
Sleep and diet disturbed; recovery ability and stress tolerance decreased

target_behavior.behavior: At work, frequently seeks reassurance from colleagues and checks repeatedly
target_behavior.core_reason: After one major mistake, formed doubts about self-ability and worry about making mistakes again and being fired (catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking)
target_behavior.function: Short-term relief of anxiety; gaining external confirmation and a sense of security
target_behavior.consequence: Relationships with colleagues are strained and efficiency declines, but anxiety recurs and is not fundamentally relieved

target_behavior.behavior: Shows strong anxiety and avoidance when facing important accounting tasks (such as choosing only low-risk tasks)
antecedent: Work situations requiring balancing accounts or handling important data
Work time approaching a task deadline
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizes one mistake into evidence of overall incompetence and predicts the worst outcome (such as being fired)
target_behavior.function: Escapes potential failure and uncertainty to reduce immediate anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, further damage to self-confidence, sleep and eating affected
